subject: pathology
title: Mesothelioma, Berylliosis, Byssinosis, Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis, Farmer Lung, and Bagassosis

steps.tx: Malignant pleural mesothelioma wraps lung in tumour rind decades after asbestos exposure, presenting with chest pain, effusion, and pleural thickening, diagnosed by thoracoscopic biopsy with mesothelial immunophenotype. The asbestos cancer is **malignant pleural mesothelioma**. This point is tested repeatedly because it changes everyday bedside decisions.
steps.say: Pleural rind, effusion, and asbestos decades ago mean mesothelioma; biopsy thoracoscopically, not blindly.

vis.caption: Malignant pleural mesothelioma encasing lung after asbestos exposure.

steps.tx: Mesothelioma markers calretinin, WT1, and cytokeratin 5/6 positivity with carcinoma marker negativity separate it from metastatic adenocarcinoma, the commonest pleural mimic demanding opposite therapy. That panel performs **mesothelioma versus adenocarcinoma immunohistochemistry**. Examiners return to it because it separates careful clinicians from guesswork.
steps.say: Calretinin and WT1 positive, carcinoma markers negative: the panel that keeps mesothelioma from adenocarcinoma's therapy.

steps.tx: Berylliosis mimics sarcoidosis granuloma for granuloma in beryllium exposed aerospace, ceramic, and electronics workers until beryllium lymphocyte proliferation testing proves sensitisation. The sarcoid twin is **chronic beryllium disease (berylliosis)**. Bedside recognition of this pattern saves time, blood, and unnecessary investigation.
steps.say: Sarcoid like granulomas plus aerospace or ceramic work demand beryllium testing before sarcoid is signed.

steps.tx: Byssinosis tightens cotton, flax, and hemp workers' chests characteristically on Monday after weekend recovery, improving across shifts, from endotoxin laden dust airway reactivity. The weekday pattern names **byssinosis (Monday fever of textile workers)**. Students should anchor this fact before moving to rarer causes and exceptions.
steps.say: Worst chest on Monday, easing by Friday: byssinosis timing betrays textile dust causation.

steps.tx: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis inflames alveoli immunologically to inhaled organic antigens, mouldy hay, bird proteins, hot tub mycobacteria, acutely with fever and breathlessness, chronically with fibrosis. The antigen driven alveolitis is **hypersensitivity pneumonitis (extrinsic allergic alveolitis)**. In practice this distinction decides the next test, treatment, or referral made.
steps.say: Fever and breathlessness hours after antigen exposure, fibrosis after years: hypersensitivity pneumonitis in two tempos.

vis.caption: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis CT patterns with mosaic attenuation and fibrosis.

steps.tx: Farmer lung from mouldy hay thermophilic actinomycetes and bagassosis from mouldy sugarcane bagasse are regional dialects of hypersensitivity pneumonitis whose names encode their antigens and occupations. Those eponyms are **farmer lung and bagassosis, occupational hypersensitivity pneumonitis**. That is why this detail earns its place in every examination and ward round.
steps.say: Farmer lung and bagassosis are hypersensitivity pneumonitis wearing occupational name tags.

steps.tx: Antigen avoidance is hypersensitivity pneumonitis therapy's foundation, steroids accelerating acute recovery without replacing removal, because continued exposure fibroses despite every drug. That hierarchy defines **antigen avoidance in hypersensitivity pneumonitis**. Remembering it prevents the commonest errors made with this presentation entirely.
steps.say: Remove the antigen or lose the lung; steroids merely hurry what avoidance alone secures.

steps.tx: Mesothelioma treatment layers surgery in highly selected early disease, chemotherapy, dual immunotherapy improving survival in unresectable disease, and meticulous palliation of effusion and pain. Multimodal selection embodies **contemporary mesothelioma management**. The clinical payoff comes from applying it early, before complications accumulate further.
steps.say: Immunotherapy changed mesothelioma survival; pleural palliation quality still decides patients' daily lives.
